text:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 - GPU queue growth / autoscaler not adding effective capacity in us-west-2. Observed queue spike at 06:12 UTC, heavy CUDA/Xid errors on multiple nodes. Paging oncall now. https://internal.ops/redwood/incidents/1749990000

oncall-jamal: I'm on it. saw alerts for queue depth +30% and >50% token latency. checking cluster metrics.

sre-alyssa: quick TL;DR from dashboards: pool-gpu-usw2 reported 80% nominal GPU count but effective available GPUs dropped ~35% since 06:05 due to driver restarts & OOMs. autoscaler attempted scale but hit API quota and some nodes failed to register (node flaps).

runtime-ryan: logs show repeated kernel driver unloads followed by container restarts. snippet:```
[06:07:11] cuda:xid=13 GPU0 -> process killed, driver reset
[06:07:13] runtime: serving loop restart; kvcache purge on node-12
```

infra-jack: cloud autoscale errors: "ExceededQuota: GPU quota 50 -> requested 60" on two scale attempts. We have reserved slots but scheduler couldn't bind due to driver health checks failing.

oncall-jamal: customer impact? support-kim?

support-kim: Delta: increased 500/5xxs across production routes; early estimate ~14% of requests saw degraded responses (timeouts or 503s) over last 8m. top affected tenants: alpha-inc, demo-saas, internal-staging. Customers on Dedicated might be more impacted if pinned to affected pool.

pm-elena: notify sales for those tenants? I'll prepare an initial message if impact confirmed. Need exact window and affected TPS.

ops-liz: mitigation proposal: 1) shift non-critical traffic to cpu-fallback or smaller model variants; 2) force drain bad nodes and restart driver; 3) temporarily increase autoscaler max (if quota allows) or request emergency quota increase; 4) enable per-customer throttles for heavy tenants.

sre-alyssa: doing steps in parallel. Jamal, Ryan - coordinate node restarts + runtime-side defensive measures.

oncall-jamal: executing: marking node-11,node-12,node-14 unschedulable and triggering drain.```bash
kubectl cordon node-11
kubectl drain node-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data -l pool=gpu-usw2
```

runtime-ryan: while drains running, I'm enabling prefix cache bypass for high-latency routes and lowering batch window to 10ms to reduce memory pressure. Patching runtime config:```json
{"batch_window_ms":10, "kv_cache_enabled": false_for_routes:["/chat/long"]}
```

infra-jack: attempted scale call #3 to add 6 GPUs => cloud error 403 "quota limit". Submitted emergency quota request — can push but not immediate. We have ondemand spare in us-east; suggestion: route burst traffic to us-east pools as fallback.

ops-liz: be careful — cross-region failover will add latency >150ms. Prefer CPU fallback for short-term.

oncall-jamal: patch applied, drains in progress. Observability: queue depth started to drop from 2200 -> 1300 in 3m. CUDA Xid errors still appear from node-14.

sre-alyssa: node-14 shows kernel logs: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 31" then GPU disappears from nvidia-smi. We're seeing correlated kernel module reloads every ~45s. Could be firmware/drivers regression deployed last night.

runtime-ryan: confirm rollback candidate: driver v525 -> v520 was rolled last week; check deploy history. If recent driver flip, revert cluster driver to v520 on affected AZ.

infra-jack: deploy history: driver-runtime-bundle:v525 pushed 02:14 UTC to all host images. Rolling back in select AZs now (us-west-2a). Starting a canary: replace host image on node-14 with v520.

support-kim: customers asking for ETA. Can we give an initial note: "We're mitigating a GPU capacity issue impacting some requests in us-west-2; engineering is working on it, will update in 30 minutes."

pm-elena: sending that now to affected accounts. keep me posted on time to resolution.

oncall-jamal: after canary rollback to v520 on node-14, node stopped crashing and registered back. queue depth further down to ~600. Still seeing sporadic 5xxs but trending down.

runtime-ryan: added temporary route-level fallback: prefix-match heavy customers -> smaller model v-small; response latency lower and avoids KV cache pressure. Applied canary traffic split 20% -> fallback.

ops-liz: autoscaler still blocked by quota. infra-jack, can you open emergency support with cloud to expedite quota lift or a temporary quota bypass?

infra-jack: raised ticket CS-94231 with cloud support, marked P1. Contacted partner rep. ETA unknown but they acknowledged.

sre-alyssa: next actions: - complete host driver rollbacks across affected AZs - keep drains until nodes stable - keep batch window low for 30m - maintain traffic fallbacks for heavy tenants - prepare postmortem with deploy diff and kernel logs.

oncall-jamal: handoff to next oncall in 30m (Ali). I'll write runbook fragment for Ali: what we did, where to look (dashboards + logs), commands to re-enable kvcache, and when to reopen autoscaler limits.

ops-liz: agree keep throttles & fallbacks for 1hr even after metrics normalize to avoid relapse.

support-kim: initial customer message sent. we'll follow up with an incident update in 45m incl root-cause if known.

pm-elena: prepping post-incident comms and CS outreach list.

incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged. Status: mitigated -> partial (queue reduced, autoscale blocked). Next update scheduled in 30m. Incident channel archived to preserve thread.

oncall-jamal: handing off to Ali now — Ali, ping me if escalation needed. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
